title: Resolving models for pullback and monoidal integer-shift squares on ring diagrams
statement:
Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings. For a scheme $W$ choose a small skeleton of its pro-etale site and put $B_{n,W}=(C_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear module systems: objects are $B_{n,W}$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_{n+1,W}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, and morphisms commute with transitions. Identify it with modules over $B_\bullet$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site and use $D(\mathscr S_W)$, the ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For a scheme morphism $v$ let $P_v$ be exact termwise inverse image. For a complex $M$, use $M[r]^p=M^{p+r}$ with differential $(-1)^r d_M$, and give $P_v$ its termwise shift comparison.

Use the canonical pullback compositors, including their inverses and the identifications from equality of scheme composites. Use the K-flat derived tensor, its canonical representative comparisons, unsigned associator $\alpha$, action unitors $\lambda,\rho$, and Koszul symmetry $\sigma(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in degrees $p,q$ [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints]. Fix $t_{a,b}:M[a]\otimes^LN[b]\cong(M\otimes^LN)[a+b]$ whose coefficient on shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ is $(-1)^{bp}$. The pullback/tensor comparison $\mu_v:P_v(M\otimes^LN)\cong P_vM\otimes^LP_vN$ is the canonical total of the ordinary pure-tensor comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

These specified comparisons admit simultaneous resolving representatives with the following properties. A pullback compositor on $M[r]$ in degree $p$ is the ordinary compositor on $M^{p+r}$, and the same holds for the identifications from equality of composites. The map representing $\mu_v$ preserves bidegrees and all coefficient transition maps; its two shift-square routes on shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ have the same coefficient $(-1)^{bp}$. Reassociation and action unitors are the unsigned rebracketing and scalar-action maps on the total models. On triple shifted degrees $(p,q,h)$ with shifts $(a,b,c)$ the two associator routes have exponents $bp+c(p+q)$ and $cq+(b+c)p$; the unitors with the degree-zero ring unit have coefficient $1$. For symmetry the representative identity is
$$\sigma_{M,N}[a+b]\,t^{M,N}_{a,b}=(-1)^{ab}t^{N,M}_{b,a}\,\sigma_{M[a],N[b]}.$$
On shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ the two exponents in this identity are $bp+(p+a)(q+b)$ and $ab+pq+aq$ (equal modulo $2$).

The representative identifications descend naturally to the specified derived system maps. For every listed map $\tau:F\to G$, every integer $r$, and any one input occurrence replaced by $M[r]$, the derived identity is $\chi_G\tau_{M[r]}=\tau_M[r]\chi_F$, where $\chi$ is the composite of the specified operation shifts; the shifted occurrence of a symmetry is followed to its permuted position. The comparisons are natural in all inputs and obey the zero-shift and addition laws in each slot, with the displayed $(-1)^{ab}$ rule for interchanging two tensor shifts. All identities hold before coefficient evaluation or restriction of scalars, including the quotient transitions when $C_n=R/t^n$. No normalized-system or cohomological boundedness assumption is imposed.
